title: Zakariyya's du'a
hook: don't leave me alone, You are the best of inheritors (21:89)

segments.voice: Yesterday, Yunus in the dark, and your line: I was wrong. Did you say it to someone, with no but after it? Today, an old man in a quiet room, asking for what looks impossible. Day six hundred ninety-three.

A sanctuary, a prayer chamber the Qur'an calls the mihrab. An old prophet named Zakariyya, the one the Bible calls Zechariah, is the guardian of a girl dedicated to God: Maryam. Surah three says that whenever he went in to her, he found food beside her that he hadn't brought. Where does this come from, he asks. From Allah, she says. And right there, the verse says, Zakariyya prayed. His hair is white. His wife has never had a child. He has no one to carry on after him. Watching that girl, he asks anyway.

The Qur'an tells his prayer more than once. Surah nineteen says he called in secret: my bones have grown weak, my head is shining with gray. Surah twenty-one gives it in one line. In Pickthall's translation: "My Lord! Leave me not childless, though Thou art the best of inheritors." Pickthall writes childless, and that is the sense. But the Arabic word is fardan, alone, single, one by himself. So the plea underneath it is the one in our line: don't leave me alone. Then comes the second half, and it is easy to hear past it. You are the best of inheritors. Everything a person leaves behind, a name, a house, a life's work, ends up with someone. Zakariyya says the One who finally inherits everything is Allah. Commentators have read that half as trust: if a son does not come, what I am is still not lost. So the prayer holds two things at once. Zakariyya asks plainly for what he wants, and says ahead of time that he will not be abandoned even if the answer is no. The next verse says the answer was yes. Allah heard him, gave him Yahya, John, and made his wife able to bear a child. And then a detail about the whole family: they hurried to do good, and called on Allah in longing and in awe. Lonely people are not rare in this book. Yunus in the fish. Ayyub in his sickness. Zakariyya in an empty house. Each of them speaks, and each is heard.
screen: `MY BONES ARE WEAK, MY HEAD IS GRAY.`
`HEARD: YAHYA, AND A FAMILY THAT HURRIED.`

segments.voice: The practice: pray for someone lonely. Sit and let your breath settle. Bring one person to mind who is more alone than they let on: an older neighbor, a friend far from home, someone newly widowed, someone at the edge of every group chat. Picture where they are right now. If you pray, you can ask for them in your own words, or borrow Zakariyya's: don't leave them alone. If you don't, simply keep them company in your mind for the length of the sit. The bell holds the time.

Zakariyya's du'a. Don't leave me alone; You are the best of inheritors. This week we went from the garden's greeting of peace to Adam, Ibrahim, Musa, Ayyub, Yunus and Zakariyya: prophets, each praying in his own trouble. Today's word.
Your line: don't leave me alone. Today, send one message to the person you held in the sit. It doesn't need a reason. Just enough so they know they were thought of. Day six hundred ninety-three.

howItsDone: Some couples hoping for a child recite Zakariyya's du'a from 21:89 and 3:38, and some Muslims also say its plea not to be left alone in times of loneliness.

myth: Zakariyya prayed while watching over Maryam
surah three says he prayed right there, after seeing her food.
the Arabic word behind 'childless' literally means alone
the Qur'an says Zakariyya never received an answer
21:90 says Allah heard him and gave him Yahya.

fork.setup: you are Zakariyya: old, gray, your wife has never had a child. you see a girl given food from nowhere. what do you do?
options: decide it's too late to ask.
pray, right there, for a child.
ask Maryam to pray for you.
fork.reveal: surah three says that right there he prayed. and he added: You are the best of inheritors, trust even if the answer were no.

original.note: Arabic: alone, single. Zakariyya asks not to be left fardan (21:89).

trapdoor: what you thought: an old man asking for a son.
what it means: don't leave me alone, and You are the best of inheritors: ask plainly, and trust that nothing is lost.
what a scholar hears: Pickthall renders fardan as childless, but the word means single, alone, so the plea is wider than an heir.

sources.quoted: My Lord! Leave me not childless, though Thou art the best of inheritors.

sources.ref: Qur'an 21:90 (heard, given Yahya, the family hurried to good)
